title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a scheme and Ω is a locally free O_S-module; it is probably the cotangent sheaf in the intended application. The page fixes an extension 0 → Ω → E --p--> O_S → 0. The previous page states that such extensions are equivalent to pairs (P, σ), where P = P(E) is the projective bundle of invertible quotients of E (Grothendieck's convention) and σ is the section given by the quotient p. It also notes that the infinitesimal neighbourhoods O_P/J^{n+1} of σ(S) are described by Sym^n.

Objects on this page.
- P̂ is the formal completion of P along σ, and Ŝ is the formal scheme with structure sheaf O_{P̂}.
- L = O_P(1) restricts to an invertible module L̂ on Ŝ.

The action of Ω. The group Ω(S) = Hom(O_S, Ω) acts on the extension by automorphisms that are the identity on both Ω and O_S. In a splitting E ≅ Ω ⊕ O_S this action is u_a(x, λ) = (x + λa, λ). Since p∘u_a = p, these automorphisms fix σ. Hence Ω acts on (P, σ), on P̂ and on Ŝ, and compatibly on L̂ as a module over the ring of scalars Ŝ.

The split case (marked °), E° ≅ Ω ⊕ O_S. An S'-point of P̂ is an invertible quotient E → L' that agrees with p over the reduced scheme. The image of the section e = (0, 1) is then a basis of L', so L' ≅ O_{S'}. The quotient therefore has the form (x, λ) ↦ φ(x) + λ, with φ: Ω → O_{S'} landing in the nilradical. This gives
- P̂° = V(Ω)^, the formal completion of the vector bundle Spec Sym(Ω) along its zero section;
- P̂° = Spf of the completed symmetric algebra Sym^(Ω) over S;
- L̂° ≅ Ŝ°.

Explicit formula for the action. Write φ̃(x, λ) = φ(x) + λ. Then
φ̃∘u_a(x, λ) = φ(x) + (1 + φ(a))λ = (1 + φ(a))·(φ/(1 + φ(a))(x) + λ).
So the transformed point is φ^a = φ/(1 + φ(a)); the factor 1 + φ(a) is invertible because φ(a) is nilpotent. The next page translates this into the action on functions: u_{a*}(f) = f/(1+a)^n for f homogeneous of degree n. It then computes the induced action on L̂.

Geometric meaning. This is the coordinate-free, scheme-theoretic form of a classical fact. The kernel of the isotropy representation of PGL_{n+1} at a point of P^n is the vector group of linear forms. It acts on the affine chart, and on the formal neighbourhood of the point, by x ↦ x/(1 + ⟨a, x⟩). This group is the abelian part of the structure group for projective connections (Cartan geometry modelled on P^n), set up here in families over S, including nilpotent directions. It is preparatory work for 'connexions projectives et uniformisation', presumably the formal model of a projective structure.
errors: No mathematical errors. The computation φ(x+λa)+λ = φ(x)+(1+φ(a))λ and the renormalization by the unit 1+φ(a) are correct; invertibility of 1+φ(a) is justified because φ takes values in the nilradical.

Minor notational looseness: Ŝ is first written as O_{P̂} (a sheaf of rings), but then used as a formal scheme on which Ω acts. Left/right conventions for the action ('à g.' vs 'à droite') are not tracked carefully; the next page passes to the transpose u_a^t.

ideas.what: Equivalence between extensions 0→Ω→E→O_S→0 and pairs (projective bundle P(E), section σ), with the formal neighbourhood of σ described by Sym(Ω)
ideas.modern_name: Projective bundle of an extension / formal neighbourhood of a section of a projective bundle
ideas.where_published: EGA II §4 for P(E) and the functor of invertible quotients; this specific equivalence as stated is not known to me in print

ideas.what: Action of Hom(O_S, Ω) = Ω(S) on the extension by unipotent automorphisms u_a(x,λ) = (x+λa, λ), inducing an action on P̂ and on L̂ = O(1)^
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism group of an extension; abelian unipotent radical of the parabolic stabilizing a point of P^n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cartan, projective geometry); standard extension theory

ideas.what: Identification of the formal completion along σ in the split case with V(Ω)^ = Spf Sym^(Ω), via the functor of points: quotients reducing to p are given by nilpotent φ: Ω → N_{S'}
ideas.modern_name: Formal completion of a vector bundle along its zero section; functor-of-points description of formal neighbourhoods
ideas.where_published: Generic EGA I/IV techniques; this specific computation is not known to me in print

ideas.what: Explicit formula φ ↦ φ/(1+φ(a)) for the action of the vector group on the formal neighbourhood (next page: f ↦ f/(1+a)^n in degree n)
ideas.modern_name: Projective (linear-fractional) action of the isotropy kernel; 'special projective transformations' fixing a point to first order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cartan's projective connections; Tanaka, Kobayashi–Nagano for the group-theoretic structure)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine scheme-theoretic rendering of the classical action of the isotropy kernel of PGL on the formal neighbourhood of a point of projective space, in families with nilpotents. It is useful preparatory work for projective connections, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'Cas E canonique (= triviale [?] i.e. on donne un plongement [?] i : O_S → E)': the image reads more like 'Cas E (= splittée/scindée, i.e. on donne q[uasi-]scindage s: O_S → E)'. It is the split case, with a splitting map labelled s, not 'i'.
'E° ≃ Ω × O_S': the × is Grothendieck's notation for the direct sum Ω ⊕ O_S (the next page writes Ω + O_S).
'homomorphisme défini' should be 'homomorphisme bien défini, de Ω dans nilradical N_S' (with 'N_S' written under 'nilradical').
'Ω opère [-à g.-]/sur Ŝ — car il opère sur l'extension (à g.) donc sur (P,σ) et P̂ (à droite)': the reading is plausible; the struck-out text over 'sur' is 'à g.'.
In 'P̂° = V(Ω)^ (complété formel le long de la section nulle) = Spf Sym^(Ω)/S°', the annotation underneath is 'L̂° ≃ Ŝ°'.
